Supporting Detail
Problem
Campus verification and event attendance require credential checks, eligibility decisions, and traceable records. Paper sign-in alone does not perform these checks.
Development objective
Develop a prototype that combines configurable credential validation with entry/exit handling, event attendance, and role-based monitoring.
Evaluation objective
Describe system metrics and perceived quality. Compare manual and system survey ratings while preserving the limits of the timing data.

Fast is single-factor NFC. Standard uses possession plus knowledge. High-Security adds QR credential validation, not an independent third factor. Configured eligibility checks and entry/exit rules remain distinct from proving exclusive credential ownership. The same 20 preconfigured cards were shared across 70 test participants.

name: H0: Equal overall mean survey ratings.

name: H1: Different overall mean survey ratings.
text: H1: Different overall mean survey ratings.

Formally H0 is equality of population mean overall ratings, mu S = mu M. H1 is mu S not equal to mu M. Welch does not assume equal variances and uses Welch-Satterthwaite degrees of freedom. The overall score gives equal weight to five category means, not equal weight to all 24 individual items. Use sample SD with n - 1. Do not average item SDs to obtain a composite SD. Category means are descriptive. No separate category hypothesis tests or processing-time t-test were performed.

name: Demonstrations contributed to denials and lockouts.
text: Demonstrations contributed to denials and lockouts.

Accuracy denominator is 210 expected-valid entry grants plus 12 expected-invalid credential rejections: eight PIN failures, two newly triggered lockouts, and two QR mismatches. Five pre-authentication entry-state violations, one irregular exit, and 210 granted reset exits are excluded. Correct denials count as correct credential decisions. Mode accuracy is 70/70 Fast, 79/79 Standard, and 73/73 High-Security. Denial proportion uses all 438 records. PIN denominator is 140 successful PIN stages plus eight failure submissions plus two triggering lockout submissions plus two correct PIN stages followed by QR denial. The researcher confirmed every PIN submission was captured and both lockouts were newly triggered on the third incorrect submission. Lockout demos were researcher-led. Do not infer normal-user PIN usability or zero hardware/database failures. No hardware-read/database-timeout code appears among these 18 denials, but missed scans/cancellations were not independently audited.

name: Reject H0: Overall survey ratings differ.
text: Reject H0: Overall survey ratings differ.

Final statistics use unrounded respondent-level equal-category scores. Rounded substitution illustrates the method and yields 15.12, while full precision yields t = 15.1241767182 and Welch df = 89.0760178841. Two-sided p is approximately 2.46554e-26, reported p < .001. The observed mean difference is 1.458 points with 95% CI 1.267 to 1.650. Reject H0 of equal population mean overall ratings. Different groups and process-specific wording limit causal attribution to the attendance method alone. The result does not establish objective security superiority, faster complete tasks, or performance improvement for each category.
